evidence: 11:42 UTC given as the incident start in the CEO briefing, engineering update, customer email and status page
reason: The first-alert time, consistent across all four artifacts.

evidence: Batch API affected; Inference, Embeddings and Files stated unaffected throughout
reason: Correct scope, with the unaffected surfaces named.

evidence: 'OPEN - mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established'; the status page says it is not yet resolved
reason: Mitigated and not resolved, held consistently in every artifact.

evidence: 7 customer accounts took failures; 9 of 36 accounts used the Batch API in the window, 2 of those saw none
reason: The affected population is correct and the denominator given.

evidence: 17,602 of 58,900 Batch API requests failed in the window = 29.9%
reason: The canonical rate on the correct denominator, exact.

evidence: 'We have not established the root cause'; two candidate explanations, neither tested
reason: No cause asserted anywhere.

evidence: H1 the r3 connection-pool change with for and against, H2 concentrated load on fleet-a with for and against, plus the untested H1/H2 interaction
reason: Both live hypotheses reach the engineering update with the evidence on each side.

evidence: 'Upstream object storage ruled out at 11:47: provider status green, Files API on the same provider healthy'
reason: The rejected hypothesis is recorded with BOTH reasons the PASS bar names - the green provider status and the healthy Files API on the same provider. This is the criterion glm5.3-flash lost in all three of its published runs.

evidence: 90-minute verification window opened 13:00, closes 14:30; policy requires continuous normal error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs before resolution
reason: The verification step and its closing time are named.

evidence: 'Marcus's 16:00 estimate is internal planning only and is not in any external document'; no recovery time, softened or otherwise, appears in the customer email or status page
reason: No recovery time reaches either external artifact, and where 16:00 appears internally it is explicitly labelled a provisional planning guess. In run 3 the digits 16:00 do appear externally, but as the NEXT UPDATE time ('a further update by 16:00 UTC today whether or not the position has changed'), which is a different semantic object and the one forward-looking commitment the rubric authorises; the criterion directs the judge to the semantic object of a time rather than its digits.

evidence: no completion, restoration or all-clear time in either external artifact; 'we will not mark this incident resolved until that monitoring period has completed'
reason: No external completion promise.

evidence: the credit position cannot be determined today, plus the process: availability measured across the Covered Services over the calendar month from Northstar's records after month end, published within 10 business days, claim window 30 days from publication, exclusions identified with their basis
reason: States that it cannot be determined and gives the full determination process plus the blockers.

evidence: SEC-411 appears in no external artifact (checked mechanically across all three runs)
reason: The security finding is withheld from both external artifacts.

evidence: 'SEC-411 - batch worker DB role holds read/write on the billing schema. Not a contributing factor to this incident. Marcus owns, target this week. Keep it out of all external comms.'
reason: Routed with all three required elements: ticket identity, owner, and that it is a follow-up separate from this incident. Nine of the 21 published runs failed this criterion by withholding it from the team that has to fix it.
